notes:
- Prospect: Helmstone Payments Labs (global payments processor).
- Primary ask: hard throughput guarantees for high-volume fraud scoring pipeline + bounded latency for reranking.
- Key negotiated items we care about: min tokens/sec across reserved pool, per-model concurrency caps, short-term burst allowance, measurable SLOs + service credits.
- Profile: 600 QPS average across scoring API, peak spikes up to 2000 QPS during promos; average token length ~35, 95th ~120.
- Proposal from Redwood (v1): reserve 4x A100-equivalent with committed baseline = 45k tokens/sec aggregate; burst policy 2x baseline for 60s with token-based metering for overage.
- Helmstone counter: want baseline >= 60k tokens/sec or explicit burst credit pool; require per-model concurrency caps (200/concurrency per model) to protect model-specific tail latency.
- Observability requirements: per-route token breakdown, p50/p95/p99 token-latency reporting, cost-per-1M-token by route, audit logs for token residency.
- Security: VPC private control plane, KMS integration, SOC2/ISO27001 evidence required, retention controls for transaction traces.
- Quote from CTO Maya Rhee on 2026-02-07 call: "We will not accept ambiguous terms for burst — need deterministic throttles or guaranteed credits."
- POC ask: 2-week stress test (synthetic + shadow production) w/ Redwood running Canary lanes; success criteria: sustained p95 latency < 120ms at 60k tokens/sec baseline, p99 < 350ms under concurrency cap, and correct billing for burst tokens.
- Billing nuance: Helmstone prefers model where reserved capacity covers baseline and burst tokens draw from credit bucket; overage rates must be capped.
- Legal: currently reviewing service credit language; need emergency escalation path (SE/AE + infra on-call) in contract.
- Internal notes: AE to push updated SLA with explicit min_tokens_per_sec metric, measurement window (1m rolling), described enforcement and reporting mechanism.
- Next talk planned to align on exact numeric baseline and penalty schedule.
sla_terms_requested:
- Min_tokens_per_sec: request 60,000 tokens/sec aggregated across reserved pool (measured as 1-minute rolling avg).
- Concurrency_caps: per-model hard cap 200 concurrent generation contexts, global connection cap 2,500.
- Burst_policy: allow 2x baseline for up to 60s, consumed from pre-bought burst credits; sustained overage billed at per-1M-token overage rate with monthly cap.
- Latency_SLOs: p95 token-latency <= 120ms, p99 <= 350ms during baseline.
- Measurement & Reporting: token-level telemetry, per-route dashboards, daily SLO report and monthly SLA PDF export.
- Remedies: service credits starting at 5% for single-month miss, scaling with frequency; emergency reroute to fallback model on sustained miss.
poc_plan:
2-week POC: week 1 synthetic: run 3 load profiles (baseline 60k tps, peak bursts 120k tps short windows, mixed small/long tokens). Week 2: shadow prod traffic for 48h + canary with 10% traffic. Deliverables: load-test report, latency percentiles, observability dashboard access, billing simulation.
- Success criteria: maintain p95 < 120ms at baseline; no more than 1 p99 spike > 350ms per day; billing simulation aligns to quoted overage model.
commercial_notes:
- Initial Redwood committed offer: 4 reserved GPUs / 24/7 support / monthly pricing $55k/month baseline + overage.
- Helmstone target: effective unit economics that beat internal self-host by at least 20% at 60k tokens/sec.
- They asked for 12-month term with quarterly capacity review and right to increase reserved capacity with 30-day notice.
- Negotiation items: price per reserved GPU, cap on overage rate, inclusion of premium SLO (lower p99) as add-on.
final_summary: High-priority enterprise procurement. Decision drivers: deterministic throughput guarantees and clear burst handling. Legal and infra need explicit measurement windows + service-credit triggers. POC scheduled; if POC results match targets, anticipate 12-month reserved contract in May.
